source.name: Form fields inside a disabled fieldset must not be treated as tabbable, so a focus-trapped dialog focuses its first usable field
source.scope: Real upstream bug (https://github.com/focus-trap/tabbable/issues/413) at cc8b7b2bc4319b672d0e6053b34c732168dd035c. Blind to the maintainers' fix 1d5fcb51d9eb21994c82a2f03010bc0d017cfff2; routing auto.

plan.root_cause: The tabbable utility incorrectly treats form controls inside a disabled fieldset as focusable because it only checks the element's own disabled property, not the inherited disabled state from a parent fieldset. This causes the focus trap to consider the disabled select as the first tabbable node, and attempting to focus it leaves focus unchanged.
plan.repair_strategy: Augment isNodeMatchingSelectorFocusable to also treat elements that match the ':disabled' pseudo-class (which includes those disabled via a parent fieldset) as not focusable.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users will now receive initial focus on the first usable field (#street) when opening the dialog, allowing them to type an address and save it.
functional_risks: Potential side effects if any other code relies on the previous behavior of considering such elements focusable; however, matching ':disabled' aligns with browser's native disabled semantics, so risk is low.
verification_requirements: After applying the edit, the journey step should pass: focus moves to #street after dialog opens.
Typing an address and saving updates the status accordingly.
Escape closes the dialog and returns focus to the opener button.
